usageNotes: Use this to move a QEMU VM from one cluster node to another; set `online: true` for live migration of a running VM (brief network blip only), or omit it to migrate an offline VM with zero downtime risk. The call returns a UPID task ID immediately — poll `get_nodes_node_tasks_upid_status` to confirm completion before treating the VM as stable on the target. If the VM has local disks and no shared storage, you must also pass `with-local-disks: true` and a valid `targetstorage` mapping, or use `force: true` (root only) to override the guard.

examples.summary: Live-migrate a running VM to another node, moving its local disk to the target's local-lvm storage

destructiveReason: Migrating with `online: false` (or when the VM is already stopped) shuts the VM down on the source node and deletes its local disk images there once copied to the target; a failed mid-migration transfer can leave disk data in an inconsistent state.
tips: Both the source and target nodes must be members of the same Proxmox cluster; cross-cluster migration is not supported via this endpoint.
For VMs on shared storage (Ceph, NFS, iSCSI) you can omit `targetstorage` entirely — the disk stays in place and only the config is moved.
Use `migration_type: insecure` only on a fully isolated, private migration VLAN to get better throughput; the default `secure` tunnels traffic over SSH.
`with-conntrack-state` is useful for stateful firewalls (e.g., Proxmox VE firewall with NAT) — migrate connection tracking entries so existing TCP sessions survive the move.
A non-zero `bwlimit` (in KiB/s) prevents the migration from saturating your management network during business hours; 102400 = 100 MB/s.
